27131:
DLG. Progress and sustainability in the agriculture and food industry
The DLG (German Agricultural Society), founded in 1885 by Max Eyth, stands for productivity and sustainability in innovation-driven improvements in agriculture and the food chain. The aim of the DLG is to promote progress through the transfer of knowledge - especially with regard to technology and quality control. Non-profit, politically independent and with an international network, the DLG has more than 30,000 members worldwide.
As one of the leading organizations in its sector, the DLG not only organizes trade fairs and events in the fields of agriculture and food technology but also tests food, agricultural technology and equipment. With its competence center for agriculture and food, its demonstration farm where practical trials take place along with its numerous publications, the DLG continually promotes independent knowledge transfer. In addition, the DLG works on numerous national and international committees of experts to develop solutions for the challenges facing agriculture and the food industry.

European Pig Producers (EPP) – A network for knowledge and exchange
The European Pig Producers (EPP) is a network of leading pig farmers dedicated to sharing experience and expertise across borders.
Pig producers in Europe operate within a shared political and economic framework. As a result, thinking in European dimensions and focusing on global trends is becoming increasingly important.
To support this development, the EPP Club was founded in 1990 in Herning, Denmark. Today, it has grown to include over 600 members from 22 countries.
The Club’s mission is to promote and strengthen the European idea within the pig farming sector.
The current President of EPP is Dutch sow farmer Gert van Beek, with German piglet producer and finisher Michael Riedl serving as Vice President.

Insighter is a science-driven feed additive company focused on advancing gut health and production performance through differentiated nutritional solutions.
We recognize that different intestinal challenges are driven by different biological mechanisms and therefore require targeted strategies. Our portfolio encompasses both antimicrobial and non-antimicrobial solutions, with selected products also providing anticoccidial activity. Antimicrobial solutions are designed to manage microbial challenges, while non-antimicrobial solutions address gut dysfunction through mechanisms that support intestinal barrier integrity, control pathological intestinal hypersecretion, improve fecal consistency, and help manage specific conditions such as CPNV-associated feed passage. Together, these differentiated mechanisms help strengthen gut resilience and support consistent production performance.
At the core of our innovation are patented delivery technologies. By applying enteric and slow-release systems to selected functional ingredients, we optimize where and how they act within the gastrointestinal tract, enhancing functional efficiency while overcoming limitations associated with conventional delivery.
This science-driven approach enables Insighter to address diverse production needs across poultry, swine, ruminants and aquaculture. Where antibiotic reduction or removal is required, our strategies offer practical alternatives to antibiotics and pharmacological levels of ZnO. In conventional production systems, the same strategies support stronger gut health and optimized production performance.
Different challenges. Different mechanisms. One integrated approach to gut health.

Furthermore, Kaeser's state-of-the-art compressor control systems with advanced IT technology take compressed air efficiency to the next level and beyond. Both users and the environment therefore benefit from the consequent energy-savings.
Subsidiaries and authorised partners in over 140 countries ensure that users are able to enjoy all of the benefits that the very best in compressed air engineering has to offer. Key markets include the EU, the United States, Latin America and the Asia-Pacific region. Kaeser owes its enviable reputation not only to the exceptional efficiency and quality of its products, but also to its reliable field service. More recently, the other industry-leading services offered by the company - such as operator models for compressed air stations, concepts within the framework of Industry 4.0 and predictive maintenance - have increasingly moved to centre stage.
Kaeser's many years of strong growth and expansion are directly attributable to its passion for innovation and strict quality standards. While your calves are fed around the clock, 24/7, you remain completely flexible in organising your daily work. This allows the automatic feeder to take your calf management to a new level.
The intuitive graphical display and connection to the mobile CalfGuide app make animal monitoring easier for you and your team. All information about your calves, status reports and alerts are always at your fingertips – both in the app and directly at the feeder.

MilkTaxi – Mobile calf feeding, designed down to the last detail
Convenient bucket feeding: The mobile milk tank enables individual calf feeding with pen identification, flexible feeding curves and dry matter calculation.
The MilkTaxi has revolutionised bucket feeding for calves. Whether calves are housed individually in calf hutches or in groups in the calf barn, the MilkTaxi allows you to feed them wherever they are. Milk replacer can be mixed reliably, while whole milk can be gently heated or pasteurised.
No more carrying heavy buckets. The manoeuvrable chassis takes care of transporting the milk to the calf pens for you. But the MilkTaxi does more than simply make your work easier. It also makes feeding more precise by ensuring that each calf receives the right amount of milk at the right temperature.
With SmartID, you can set up individual feeding curves that allow calves to be weaned gradually and gently. The connection to the CalfGuide management system gives you full control over workflows in the calf barn and enables detailed documentation of milk preparation and calf feeding. And as an added bonus, feeding calves with the MilkTaxi is simply fun!
NativeCalfConcept
Our concept for natural and healthy calf rearing – and how you can benefit from improved animal welfare.
Automation and digitalisation are key topics in modern calf rearing. The aim is to make everyday processes as time-efficient and cost-effective as possible. At the same time, however, calf rearing is moving further and further away from the way calves would naturally grow and develop.
This is an understandable part of the transition towards modern farming – but is it really the best approach? Are we perhaps overlooking important things that nature simply does better? What can – or must – we learn from nature to raise healthy calves and help them develop into high-performing dairy cows? And how can we apply these insights to “conventional” calf rearing?
The Holm & Laue NativeCalfConcept provides answers to these questions. The good news is that a more natural approach to calf rearing pays off in many ways. With a few sensible adjustments and targeted investments, you can take your calf management to the next level!

Murska disc and roller mills are designed for producing crimped fodder on livestock farms. Crimping is a method by which the grain is flattened without drying and stored in airtight conditions, like silage. The green fodder method increases milk and meat yields, significantly reduces costs and is environmentally friendly.
Crimped grain has a higher nutritional value than feed ground from dry grain. Grain crimping also reduces mycotoxin levels.
Crimped grain can be stored in airtight plastic tubes, bunkers, horizontal silos, clamps or tower silos. Bagging crimped grain in plastic tubes is a low-cost and simple storage method.

Unibio is a biotechnology company specialising in gas fermentation. Our flagship product is Uniprotein®, a high-quality, non-GMO single-cell protein for animal feed, produced by gas fermentation using methane as the carbon source. With 68.5% crude protein, a favourable amino acid profile, high digestibility and consistent batch-to-batch quality, Uniprotein® is a proven alternative to fishmeal and soy protein concentrate in diets for weaned piglets, poultry, fish and shrimp, as well as in premium petfood.
Uniprotein® is a scalable, nutrient-rich and planet-friendly protein source. Producing it uses very little water, requires no arable land, and eases pressure on wild fish stocks, protecting both terrestrial and marine ecosystems. We are committed to changing how protein is made, through innovation and responsible production that serves future generations.
Uniprotein® is made using our proprietary U-Loop® bioreactor, a technology built for efficient, large-scale gas fermentation. Production is modular and can be sited wherever methane is available.
Deutsch
Unibio ist ein Biotechnologieunternehmen mit Spezialisierung auf Gasfermentation. Unser Hauptprodukt ist Uniprotein®, ein hochwertiges, nicht gentechnisch verändertes Einzellerprotein (Single Cell Protein) für die Tierernährung, das durch Gasfermentation mit Methan als Kohlenstoffquelle gewonnen wird. Mit 68,5 % Rohprotein, einem günstigen Aminosäurenprofil, hoher Verdaulichkeit und gleichmäßiger Qualität von Charge zu Charge ist Uniprotein® eine erprobte Alternative zu Fischmehl und Sojaproteinkonzentrat, sowohl in Futtermitteln für Absetzferkel, Geflügel, Fische und Garnelen als auch in Premium-Petfood.
Uniprotein® ist eine skalierbare, nährstoffreiche und umweltfreundliche Proteinquelle. Die Herstellung benötigt sehr wenig Wasser, keine Ackerfläche und entlastet die Wildfischbestände, was Land- und Meeresökosysteme schützt. Wir arbeiten daran, die Proteinherstellung neu zu denken: mit Innovation und verantwortungsvoller Produktion im Sinne kommender Generationen.
Uniprotein® entsteht in unserem firmeneigenen U-Loop®-Bioreaktor, einer Technologie für effiziente Gasfermentation im industriellen Maßstab. Die Produktion ist modular und lässt sich überall dort errichten, wo Methan verfügbar ist.

From individual animals to global responsibility: in the agricultural science programs at TUM, you’ll gain insights into all fields of agricultural science. Over the course of your studies, you can choose your own area of focus: animal husbandry and health, agricultural engineering, agricultural economics, crop production, digitalization in agriculture, and many more.
In the master’s programs, you’ll find even more specialized tracks: Agricultural Systems Science, Agricultural Biosciences, or perhaps International Agricultural Policy and Governance? Additionally, depending on your program, you can earn up to 65 of your 120 credits through elective courses. Numerous project-based assignments and study abroad opportunities allow you to gain many new insights—beyond the lecture hall—that will enrich your personal and professional life.
Stop by booth 13E57 to speak directly with TUM students and learn more!
Studying in Freising, the City with the Cathedral and the University
The agricultural sciences program at TUM is primarily based on the Freising-Weihenstephan campus, but TUM has close ties to many universities worldwide—apply for a study abroad program and get even more out of your studies.
Current research projects: Thermoregulation of calves and energy management
At the booth, we’ll also be presenting current research projects from the Chair of Animal Nutrition and Metabolism led by Prof. Julia Steinhoff-Wagner. For example, we’re looking at thermoregulation in calves: calf blankets, straw bedding, or being licked dry by the mother? What’s the best way to support the calf? These and many other questions are being investigated at TUM.
Fredrik Regler from the Chair of Agricultural Systems Engineering, headed by Prof. Heinz Bernhardt, will present the H2Cow project. H2Cow is an energy management concept that, among other things, investigates the storage of excess PV electricity. The project aims to contribute to the further electrification of agriculture.

#1 in Germany
#7 worldwide
Shanghai Global Rankings of Academic Subjects in Agricultural Sciences
Agricultural Science Degree Programs Offered:
- Bachelor of Science in Agricultural Sciences and Horticultural Sciences
- Master of Science in Agricultural Systems Sciences

Stay up to date with agricultural sciences at TUM: the Hans Eisenmann Forum
The Hans Eisenmann Forum brings together agricultural science expertise on campus. Named after Hans Eisenmann, who also studied at the Freising campus and went on to become Minister of Agriculture, the Hans Eisenmann Forum is the central hub for agricultural science topics at TUM. If you’d like to stay informed about agricultural sciences on campus, follow us on social media and visit our website!
We offer various on-site events that you can attend on campus. You can already participate online in the Hans Eisenmann Academy, where you can learn about the latest developments in agricultural sciences.

About Eurofins Genomics - Agrigenomics Business Line
Eurofins Genomics’ Agrigenomics portfolio provides genomic solutions for plant, livestock and aquaculture breeding programmes. As part of Eurofins Genomics, the genomic division of the Eurofins Scientific Group, it supports customers with flexible, scalable DNA sequencing, genotyping and bioinformatics services across the entire breeding workflow. Its portfolio spans DNA marker discovery, targeted and sequencing-based genotyping, low-pass whole-genome sequencing, marker-assisted and genomic selection, parentage verification, and microbiome and metagenomics analysis. Using qPCR-, microarray- and NGS-based platforms, the Agrigenomics team develops tailored solutions for a broad range of species, including complex, polyploid and poorly characterised genomes. Backed by Eurofins Genomics’ international network, high-throughput capabilities, scientific expertise and dedicated project support help breeders and research organisations turn genomic data into timely, reliable breeding decisions. For further information, please visit the Eurofins Genomics website.

The nationwide Fokus Tierwohl network was established to provide long-term support to livestock farmers in Germany and to help them prioritise animal welfare, environmental protection, production quality and market orientation.
The joint project aims to improve the transfer of knowledge into practice in order to make pig, poultry and cattle farms in Germany fit for the future in terms of animal-welfare-friendly, environmentally sound and sustainable livestock farming.
For the first time, this network brings together specialist knowledge, organises the exchange of experience between practitioners, scientists, consultants and other groups, and thereby facilitates and promotes knowledge-sharing within the sector.
Over a period of three years, a wide range of events across Germany will be used to convey to livestock farmers the consolidated, processed and focused knowledge on animal-welfare-friendly husbandry of cattle, pigs and poultry. The consolidation of scientific data, the latest findings from applied research, practical experience, animal welfare model and demonstration projects (MuD) or other current projects takes place in species-specific offices. These offices collect and process the latest data in close coordination with the network partners and make it available to project partners in the federal states for knowledge transfer.
The Focus on Animal Welfare network is embedded within the Federal Livestock Farming Programme. The Federal Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Home Affairs (BMLEH) has commissioned the Federal Office for Agriculture and Food (BLE) to act as the project sponsor.

Als 2010 Herr Xaver Hierl (RBG Memmingen) und Herr Hans Mair (Tiroler Braunviehzuchtverband) die Zeichen der Zeit erkannten und die Gründung der Alpengenetik eG vereinbarten, waren schnell ein paar Grundsätze klar. Neben der engeren europäischen Zusammenarbeit sollte das Ziel sein, den Mitgliedern eine breite Palette an Top-Braunviehgenetik zu günstigen Preisen anbieten zu können. Auch wollte man den einzelbetrieblichen Bedürfnissen in Bezug auf ihr persönliches Zuchtziel bestmöglich gerecht werden, damit die Mitgliedsbetriebe auch in Zukunft auf die Herausforderungen der modernen Landwirtschaft vorbereiten.
So stand der Gründung am 07. Juni 2010 nichts mehr im Wege, um die gemeinsame Vision mit Leben zu erfüllen. Mit Beitritt des Vorarlberger Braunviehzuchtverbands im Oktober 2011, sowie der Kärntener Braunviehzüchter im April 2012 wurde die Alpengenetik eG zum größten Braunvieh-Genetikanbieter der EU. Über alle Organisationen hinweg kann die Alpengenetik auf über 150.000 Brown Swiss Herdebuchkühe in etwa 13.500 Mitgliedsbetrieben zurückgreifen.
Die züchterischen Erfolge ließen gemäß den Erwartungen ebenfalls nicht lange auf sich warten: Bereits ab 2010 waren genomische Spitzenstiere wie AG Halleluja (der erste Stier der AG), AG Vanpari, AG Puck, AG Hegall und AG Voice im breiten Einsatz verfügbar und konnten mit ihren hervorragenden Vererberqualitäten Verkaufszahlen im fünfstelligen Bereich realisieren.
Bis heute hat sich der Erfolg der 2010 gegründeten Kooperation weiter fortgesetzt.Nachdem 2019 alle Stiere in die neu gebauten Stallungen der Rinderbesamungs-Genossenschaft Memmingen eG in Hitzenhofen umgezogen sind, hat sich das Stierangebot der Alpengenetik um weitere Größen wie AG Bison, AG Vpower, AG Vollmacht und AG Pirol aufgebaut. 25 Jahre nach Gründung kann man eines mit Sicherheit auch für die Zukunft der Alpengenetik sagen: Die beste Genetik aus vier Verbänden unter dem Dach der Alpengenetik wird auch künftig für hervorragende Braunviehqualität stehen!

ADDINOL is one of the few independent, medium-sized companies in the German mineral oil industry that is represented by distribution partners in more than 120 countries across all continents. Our high-performance lubricants are components that represent the very cutting edge of modern technology. They are developed and produced in accordance with the very latest standards at the historic chemical site in Leuna, in central Germany. Working in harmony with engines, drives, chains, bearings and hydraulic systems, they deliver their full range of performance in a targeted manner.
ADDINOL offers intelligent solutions that ensure optimum lubrication whilst guaranteeing a responsible approach to the environment. Many of our high-performance lubricants significantly improve the energy efficiency of plant and engines. They offer considerably longer service life than conventional products and extend the service life of the lubricated components.
The lubrication of stationary gas engines for operation with natural gas and special gases is one of our core areas of expertise. ADDINOL offers the right lubricant for every application and all operating conditions.
Whether operating on natural gas or special gases – the advantages of ADDINOL gas engine oils speak for themselves:
- stable operation and long engine service life
- maximum engine cleanliness
- exceptionally long service life – up to 50 per cent longer than conventional gas engine oils
- reliable protection against wear, deposits and corrosion
- precisely tailored maximum oil service life
- comprehensive analysis service
- maximum operational reliability
- the right product for all types of gas and operating conditions
- approved by leading international engine manufacturers
The use of gas engine oils is supported by the ADDINOL analysis service. Based on regular monitoring of key parameters, conclusions can be drawn regarding the condition of the oil and the plant. Optimal change intervals are determined, ensuring maximum operational safety.
Engines and gearboxes in agricultural machinery and tractors, hydraulic power units, bearings and compressors are also reliably lubricated with high-performance lubricants made in Leuna. Vehicles and machinery used in agriculture and forestry must deliver full performance at all times, even under the most extreme conditions. Reliable and safe lubrication is therefore essential. High wear protection during long periods of operation, long-term corrosion protection and biodegradability are just a few examples of the complex requirements placed on lubricants. ADDINOL offers optimal lubrication solutions for all applications, ranging from tractors, harvesters and commercial vehicles, through stationary and mobile hydraulic systems, to milking machines, saws and transport equipment. The ADDINOL NatureProof range also provides biodegradable lubricants for use in environmentally sensitive areas.

Holoruminant is a multi-actor project aiming to elucidate the role of ruminant-associated microbiomes and their interplay with the host animal in early life and throughout fundamental life events (e.g. weaning, feed transitions and lactation) that are known to affect health, welfare and environmental efficiency in ruminant production systems. HoloRuminant will use a holistic multi-omics approach to characterize the establishment and dynamics of microbiomes. In this way, HoloRuminant will determine the connectivity between microbiomes from different body sites, their heritability and their influence on the host’s key performance indices (KPIs) of efficiency of production, growth, resistance to disease, methane emissions, carbon footprint and phenotypic resilience to changing environmental conditions. The main outputs of the project will be the creation of an expandable benchmark dataset of ruminant-associated microbes, microbiomes and methods for analysis that will be used for answering essential (who, what, where and when) scientific questions and will be the knowledge foundation for innovation.

NKTEK develops solutions for dairy cow health monitoring that step in exactly where current practices reach their limits. Growing herd sizes and labor shortages make continuous, manual health monitoring nearly impossible! That is why we developed HerdTek. The system is based on a ear device attached just like a standard ear tag. It continuously measures seven vital parameters directly on the animal, including in-depth cardiovascular parameters such as heart rate, heart rate variability, and respiratory rate. This enables a comprehensive health profile for each individual animal with an unprecedented depth of data. About Reap Interactive
Reap Interactive is an Irish agri-tech company building precision livestock monitoring for beef and dairy herds. We set out to turn a weighing device into a management system, so farmers have the information to decide what to do next with every animal and not just a number to glance at. Our founder grew up farming in Roscommon and trained in computer science. He saw a gap in how individual animals were monitored and built Reap to close it.
How it works
Reap systems are installed in the pen with the animals. Every time an animal drinks, it is weighed and identified by their EID tag. The animal comes to the technology, so there's no extra handling and no extra labour. Weight, water intake and activity data go automatically to our web platform, giving farmers a continuous view of every animal, with clear, easy to read insight on herd performance and on high and low performers.
Our products:
Bovine Junior - monitoring from birth to 12 months, built for calf health and early detection.
 Bovine Plus - monitoring from 12 months through to finishing, for beef and dairy herds.
 Both systems can be configured for outdoor use, so the same approach works on pasture as well as in the shed.
Who we work with
Reap works directly with commercial farmers, from family herds to large finishing operations. We also work with research and education institutions, and our systems are installed at leading Irish research sites and agricultural colleges, where accurate, consistent data matters most.
Recognition

REALDYME® – standardised, fermentable fibre for young animal nutrition
Since 1978, REALDYME has been transforming plant materials through industrial micronisation in France. Our core material is a defined blend of selected wheat fractions. Micronisation changes their physical structure. It increases the contact surface, opens up the fibrous structure and makes the fibre progressively fermentable.
REALDYME® Feed is a standardised fermentable fibre for the sensitive phases of young animals:
 • Piglets – supporting the intake loop from creep feed to starter, and digestive resilience around weaning
 • Starter poultry – feeding the caeca from day one, with a particle size designed for caecal access, supporting early caecal fermentation
 • Calves – supporting the transition from milk to plant-based feed, with easy use in milk replacers
Recommended inclusion rate: 1%.
REALDYME® Feed complements other formulation levers (acidification, structural fibres, protein management) without replacing them. Used in Europe and Asia, it has been evaluated in a wide range of contexts, from experimental stations to commercial farms.
Beyond animal nutrition, our expertise also serves human food (IBM® for breadmaking and fibre enrichment, and the Doses-O-Son food supplement) and contract micronisation.
